recipe.title: Gobi Paratha (Cauliflower Paratha)

ingredients.name: 1 cup grated boiled potato (potatoes must be boiled and refrigerated a day in advance)
ingredients.prep_note: grated; potatoes must be boiled and refrigerated a day in advance

steps.text: Mix flour, salt, and oil in a large mixing bowl. You can also use a parat (Indian utensil) to knead the dough.
steps.label: Make dough

steps.text: Gradually add water (approx 3/4 cup) and knead to make a soft dough. The exact amount of water will depend on the quality of the flour. Do not add much water in one go; otherwise, the dough can become sticky.
steps.label: Knead dough

steps.text: Knead the dough for 2-3 minutes until it is smooth.
steps.label: Knead 2–3 min

steps.text: Note – You can knead the dough with a stand mixer fitted with a dough attachment.
steps.label: Stand mixer note
steps.role_cue: Note 013 You can knead the dough with a stand mixer fitted with a dough attachment.

steps.text: Cover the dough with a kitchen cloth and keep aside on the counter for 20 minutes.
steps.label: Rest dough
steps.attention_cue: keep aside on the counter for 20 minutes.

steps.text: Add cauliflower, boiled potatoes, green chilies, cilantro, ginger, salt, and garam masala powder to a medium-sized mixing bowl and mix nicely.
steps.label: Make stuffing
consumes_ingredients: 1 cup grated boiled potato (potatoes must be boiled and refrigerated a day in advance)

steps.text: Do not add the salt if you are not making the paratha immediately. Once mixed with salt, cauliflower releases water, making the filling moist and difficult to stuff.
steps.label: Salt caution
steps.role_cue: Do not add the salt if you are not making the� paratha immediately.

steps.text: Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Make smooth balls from the pieces and press them gently.
steps.label: Divide dough

steps.text: Take one dough ball and dust it with some dry flour. Keep the remaining dough balls covered with a kitchen cloth to prevent them from drying.
steps.label: Prepare ball

steps.text: Roll it using a rolling pin into a 5-inch disc.
steps.label: Roll disc

steps.text: Keep 2 tbsp filling in the center of the disc and bring the ends together. Shape the stuffed dough to make a smooth ball.
steps.label: Stuff dough

steps.text: Dust again with dry flour and gently roll to make a 6-inch disc. Apply light and even pressure while rolling; otherwise, the paratha can break. Go from one side to another while rolling and keep dusting with dry flour if gobi paratha sticks to the rolling pin or surface. Roll the edges slightly thinner than the center.
steps.label: Roll paratha

steps.text: Tip – If the paratha tears from someplace, sprinkle some dry flour and tap lightly.
steps.label: Tear tip
steps.role_cue: Tip 013 If the paratha tears from someplace, sprinkle some dry flour and tap lightly.

steps.text: Heat a griddle (tawa) over medium heat. When hot, transfer the paratha to the griddle.
steps.label: Heat griddle

steps.text: Cook till brown spots appear on the lower side (1-2 minutes).
steps.label: Cook first side
steps.doneness_cue: brown spots appear on the lower side

steps.text: Flip the paratha and cook until brown spots appear on the other side (1-2 minutes). Flip again.
steps.label: Cook second side
steps.doneness_cue: brown spots appear on the other side

steps.text: Apply 1 tsp ghee or oil on each side and cook the gobi paratha till golden brown. Keep pressing while cooking with the back of a ladle to make it crispy from the outside.
steps.label: Fry with ghee

steps.text: Make all the parathas in the same manner. Serve hot with white butter and achar.
steps.label: Serve
